A 228-catchment paper cannot be the source for a 472-catchment dataset, a 242-catchment subset, or any of the gauge attributes quoted. Cite 10.5281/zenodo.14999580 for the data and the ESSD DOI only for the method.

rejected.name: CLAIM: CHIRPS-GEFS v12 is 'still updating in 2026'
rejected.reason: REJECTED - it stopped two months ago. The 2026/ directory contains only month directories 01/ through 06/, and 2026/06/ ends at day 30/. That matches the README's own notice, which the sweep quoted but treated as future tense: 'CHIRPS2-GEFS will be discontinued on July 1, 2026.' The 2021 archive is unaffected and still serves, so the source itself stands - but the metadata is stale, and the migration is a live risk to the download_hint: /products/CHIRPS-GEFS/v2/ and /v3/ both return 200 today with a DIFFERENT directory schema (05_day/, 10_day/, 15_day/, daily/, dekad_lead_0/, pentad_lead_0..2/, plus 16_day/ in v3), so the daily_16day/YYYY/MM/DD/data.YYYY.MMDD.tif pattern will not survive the move.

rejected.name: CLAIM: Caravan-MultiMet CHIRPS_GEFS spans '~1999-2023' with an '18,656-entry basin index'
rejected.reason: REJECTED on both numbers, from decoded coordinates rather than metadata inference. The date coordinate has 8,797 contiguous daily values and decodes to 2000-01-01 through 2024-01-31 - the 'days since 1999-01-01' epoch is not the first date, the first value is offset 365. The basin dimension is 18,655, matching the composition counts which sum to exactly 18,655; the 18,656 figure is 4 chunks x 4,664 including chunk padding and does not exist in the data. lead_time decodes to [1..16], not [0..15]. None of this touches the India-absence finding, which I independently reconfirmed.

rejected.name: CLAIM: GRRR gives 'error-bearing DISCHARGE ... at 0-7 day lead' (source 4 relevance, key_finding 1, technology 2)
rejected.reason: REJECTED AT LEAD 0 - THIS IS THE PART (D) TRAP HIDING INSIDE AN OTHERWISE CLEAN SOURCE. Google's own documentation states the identity 'Reanalysis[time=T] == Reforecast[time=T+1, lead_time=0]'. lead_time=0 is therefore not a forecast at all: it is the reanalysis value for the day that has just ended, produced from observed CPC/IMERG precipitation. Any benefit-retention curve that starts at lead 0 will show a suspiciously strong first point that is really observed-rainfall-driven discharge - the same perfect-foresight leak the whole exercise exists to remove. Score from lead 1 upward and say so. The GRRR technology note already uses '1, 3, 5 and 7 day lead', which is correct; it is the source-level '0-7 day lead' phrasing that must be fixed before anyone writes the loader.

rejected.name: CLAIM: the Google Flood Forecasting method surface 'was mapped with a clean 403-vs-404 oracle on floodforecasting.googleapis.com (403 = real method needing a key, 404 = no such path)'
rejected.reason: REJECTED AS A METHOD. The oracle is HTTP-verb dependent and therefore not clean. floodStatus:searchLatestFloodStatusByArea, significantEvents:search and flashFloods:search all return 404 on GET and 403 only on POST. Conversely serializedPolygons:get returned 404 on both GET and POST from that host, yet Google's own REST reference lists serializedPolygons as a v1 resource with a get method - so a 404 from this endpoint does not establish non-existence. The entry's list of 'confirmed non-existent' paths (gauges:queryLatestFloodStatusByArea, gaugeModels:searchGaugeModelsByArea, gaugeForecasts:queryGaugeForecasts, inundationMaps:batchGet) may well be right, but it is not established by this test. The archive floors, which are the decision-relevant part, ARE confirmed from the documentation and stand.

rejected.name: CLAIM: GEFS 'APCP in pgrb2s is an ACCUMULATION over a 6 h window'
rejected.reason: REJECTED AS STATED - it is a 6-hourly-RESETTING accumulation sampled at both 3 h and 6 h, and taking the caveat literally produces double counting. Verified from the .idx sidecars for gep01 on 2021-10-15 00z: f003 '0-3 hour acc fcst', f006 '0-6 hour acc fcst', f021 '18-21 hour acc fcst', f024 '18-24 hour acc fcst', f027 '24-27 hour acc fcst'. Summing the 3-hourly files as if each were disjoint double counts the first half of every 6-hour window. Either use only the f006/f012/f018/... records as disjoint 6-h totals, or difference within each window (the f0N6 value minus the f0N3 value). This is a concrete ingestion bug waiting to happen in step (1) of the recommended workflow.

rejected.name: CLAIM: the Open-Meteo ensemble response is 'a LIST of per-model objects; each has hourly with 83 keys of the form precipitation_...'
rejected.reason: REJECTED as described. The live call with models=gfs025,ecmwf_ifs025 returned a single JSON OBJECT (not a list) with one hourly block containing 83 keys, of which 'time' is one and 82 are precipitation series (31 GFS: mean plus member01-30; 51 IFS: mean plus member01-50). An ingester written from 'a list of per-model objects, 83 precipitation keys each' will fail on the first call and, if it silently coerces, will mis-count members. Everything else in the entry - the 9.75/77.0/737.0 m grid snap, the roughly 79,974-byte payload, the rolling-window rejection of 2021 - reproduced exactly.

rejected.name: CLAIM: the Open-Meteo ERA5 reference series for Idukki, 'daily precipitation_sum for 2021-10-12..18 returned [55.50, 7.90, 10.60, 2.90, 33.00, 34.60, 8.60] mm', as written in the download_hint
rejected.reason: REJECTED AS AN IRREPRODUCIBLE RECIPE - the numbers are real but the call that produces them is not the one given. The hint's URL has no timezone parameter, and run that way it returns [40.2, 12.6, 5.4, 4.9, 45.0, 21.8, 7.9]. The quoted values appear only with &timezone=Asia/Kolkata. Adding &models=era5 (i.e. actual ERA5 rather than the default era5_seamless blend) gives a third answer, [26.9, 2.7, 5.8, 2.7, 65.2, 30.6, 8.6], and &models=era5_land returns all nulls at this location. Three defaults, three different 'truth' series, up to 40% apart on individual days. If this is used to bias-correct GEFS, pin timezone and models explicitly, and do not call the default product 'ERA5'.

rejected.name: CLAIM: Nearing et al. state that 'the comparison favours the GloFAS benchmark' because GloFAS could only be benchmarked at 0-day lead
rejected.reason: REJECTED on the reason, not the quote. The quote is verbatim, but the paper attributes it to the evaluation split, not the lead time: 'metrics for GloFAS were calculated over a combination of gauged and ungauged locations, and over a combination of calibration and validation time periods. This means that the comparison favours the GloFAS benchmark. This is necessary because calibrating GloFAS is computationally expensive...'. A minor point on its own, but this paper is the intellectual licence for using a GRRR virtual gauge at Idukki, so its caveats should be quoted accurately.

rejected.name: CLAIM: NeuralHydrology 'modelzoo/ contains 25 files'
rejected.reason: REJECTED as a count - the GitHub contents API returns 26 entries. Every named module is present, so nothing downstream changes; recorded only because the sweep presented it as a counted fact and the same counting habit produced the 243-catchment and 18,656-basin errors above.

verification_notes: PART (D) - THE HEADLINE ANSWER. The analysis-masquerading-as-forecast trap is NOT present in the sources this sweep recommends, and the sweep deserves credit for actively hunting it. I re-ran its detection independently and it reproduces exactly: the Open-Meteo Historical Forecast API returns 24 hourly precipitation values for 2021-10-15 but precipitation_previous_day3 is 0 of 24 populated for 2021-10-15 and 0 of 24 for 2022-07-15, against 24 of 24 for both 2024-07-15 and 2024-04-15; and the daily variant errors verbatim with 'Cannot initialize ForecastVariableDaily from invalid String value precipitation_previous_day3_sum'. The lead-time archive really does begin in early 2024, and for 2021 that endpoint really would have served what amounts to an analysis. Positively, the two recommended hindcast sources pass a provenance test I ran myself: GEFS objects for gefs.20211015/00z carry LastModified 2021-10-15T03:47Z, and CHIRPS-GEFS data.2021.1018.tif carries Last-Modified Fri, 15 Oct 2021 20:52:22 GMT - both written on the issue date, so both are genuinely contemporaneous.

PART (D), THE RESIDUAL LEAK THE SWEEP MISSED. GRRR carries a smaller version of the same trap, documented in the very notebook the sweep read. Google states 'Reanalysis[time=T] == Reforecast[time=T+1, lead_time=0]', so lead_time=0 IS the reanalysis, driven by observed CPC/IMERG precipitation. Evaluating benefit retention at lead 0 reintroduces near-perfect foresight through the back door and would produce a flattering first point on the decay curve. Separately, and newly quoted here, the GRRR reforecast is driven by 'HRES and GraphCast weather forecasts that were issued until time T', with Google explicitly noting 'We ignore the realistic delay of several hours in obtaining the data which exists in an operational setting'. GraphCast did not exist in 2021, so its 2021 fields are necessarily ERA5-initialised re-runs: causal, but a 2023-generation model with better-than-operational initial conditions and no data latency. The sweep's instinct to label GRRR an optimistic bound is right; the mechanism is now nameable and quotable.

THE STRONGEST FINDING IN THE SWEEP IS ALSO ITS BIGGEST OVERCLAIM. Everything in the GEFS entry checks out byte for byte - the .idx offset 8942680, the 268,556-byte 206 response beginning 'GRIB', gep30 present at f240, 404 at f243, four cycles a day, bucket root at gefs.20170101. This is real and it does close the perfect-foresight gap. But key_finding 5's headline, 'the Western Ghats are measurably the worst place in India to forecast rain', inverts its own source: Durai et al. report that anomaly correlation DECREASES from the west coast to the east coast in all four EPS, i.e. the west coast scores BEST on their skill metric, while the 25-30 mm/day RMSE is large because west-coast rainfall is large (their observed field peaks at about 15 mm/day over the Konkan coast). Nitha et al., now read in full, independently show a non-catastrophic regime over Kerala at day 1-3 (CSI 0.49-0.57, ECMWF FAR 0.41). Fix the framing to 'absolute errors are about double the all-India value because the rainfall is about double' before this goes into a report.

THE 789-VERSUS-792 DISPUTE IS SETTLED IN FAVOUR OF THIS SWEEP, WHICH MEANS AN ALREADY-CONFIRMED FILE IS WRONG. Per-page extraction of the Current Science PDF puts the POD sentence on PDF page 13, which bears the running number 792; PDF page 10 bears 789 and contains no such text. research/raw/soa-limitations.verify.json currently records 'THE HEADLINE FORECAST-SKILL CLAIM IS CONFIRMED VERBATIM (p.789)' and repeats p.789 in its verification notes. That entry needs correcting, or the two verify files will contradict each other in the synthesis.

A SECOND CITATION DEFECT IN THE SAME CHAIN, ORIGINATING WITH SUDHEER ET AL. Their reference 23 is given as 'Geofizika, 2013, 30, 119-141'. The Hrcak table of contents for Geofizika Vol. 30 No. 2 (2013) shows that Durai & Bhardwaj's 'Improving precipitation forecasts skill over India using a multi-model ensemble technique' is on pages 155-172, while 119-141 is Ooi & Mandeep on Malaysian rainfall-rate conversion. The sweep copied the error and then declared the paper unretrievable. It is retrievable at hrcak.srce.hr/clanak/171593, bot-blocked only on the file endpoint (HTTP 418). If AquaSync cites the primary source of the 20-30% POD figure, cite 30(2), 155-172, and read it first.

THE DEAD-END LIST COST THE PROJECT ITS BEST OBSERVED-RAINFALL PRODUCT. dead_end 16 rejects the IMD 0.25 deg gridded rainfall NetCDF page on a curl 000, but the page returns 200 and a single POST of 'RF25=2021' to /cmpg/Griddata/RF25.php returns ind2021_rfp25.nc, 25,431,832 bytes, valid NetCDF, in one call - I did it. That is the gauge-based national product against which CAMELS-IND, Durai et al. and Nitha et al. all validate, and it is the right bias-correction target over the Ghats. The sweep's fallback, ERA5 through Open-Meteo, is a reanalysis with three different default flavours (see the rejected entry) and is strictly the weaker choice. Two other dead ends are also softer than stated: dead_end 10 (MDPI) has two working routes and dead_end 9 (Geofizika) has one. The pattern is identical each time - one failing URL treated as proof of unavailability.

THE GENUINELY HARD REJECTIONS ALL SURVIVE RE-TEST, AND THAT MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE CORRECTIONS. Open-Meteo ensemble for 2021 (rolling window now reported as 2026-05-27 to 2026-10-02); ECMWF Open Data (exactly four date directories today, AWS mirror floor 20230118); NOAA GEFSv12 retrospective (year prefixes 2000 through 2020 and stop, so it misses the case study by one year); Caravan/MultiMet (zero Indian basins, decoded from the blosc chunks rather than assumed); CHIRPS-GEFS (no per-member directory anywhere in the tree); Google Flood Forecasting API (2023-10-01 and 2025-08-01 floors quoted from the live reference docs); and the digital-twin and PINN rejections, whose supporting facts all re-check within normal drift (eclipse-ditto/ditto 920 stars EPL-2.0 pushed 2026-08-28; NVIDIA/physicsnemo 3206 stars Apache-2.0 pushed 2026-08-27; github.com/NVIDIA/modulus 301-redirects to physicsnemo; docs.nvidia.com/physicsnemo/ returns 404; maziarraissi/PINNs 6114; lululxvi/deepxde 4390 LGPL-2.1; NVIDIA/physicsnemo-sym 334). The reasoning behind rejecting a digital-twin platform for a two-reservoir system, and behind rejecting PINN surrogates for an already-instantaneous forward model, is sound and should be kept as a stated finding rather than hedged.

THE CAMELS-IND PERIYAR RESULT IS THE MOST IMPRESSIVE PIECE OF WORK IN THE SWEEP AND IT SURVIVES INDEPENDENT REPLICATION. I re-derived it from scratch by parsing both ZIP central directories over HTTP Range and inflating the attribute tables: 472 forcing files in the full archive, exactly 32 basin-15 catchments with contiguous ids 15001-15032, and Neeleswaram / Vandiperiyar / Arangaly matching on name, river, latitude, longitude, area, mean elevation and flow availability to every decimal quoted. The forcing header confirms 19 variables from 1980-01-01. Only the subset count (242, not 243) and the choice of the ESSD DOI as the source URL are wrong.

TWO ITEMS ARE STALE RATHER THAN FALSE, AND BOTH ARE ON A CLOCK. CHIRPS-GEFS v12 stopped updating on 2026-06-30 and its archive is scheduled to move to a path with a different directory schema; the ECDS TIGGE temporal extent has advanced to 2026-08-26. Neither affects the October 2021 use case, but the CHIRPS-GEFS download_hint will break, so mirror what you need from the EWX tree now rather than assuming the path persists.

WHAT THE SWEEP DID NOT VERIFY AND SHOULD NOT BE QUOTED AS VERIFIED. The claim that GEFSv12 became operational on 2020-09-23 is presented as fact but is not established by anything in the S3 bucket - it needs an NCEP implementation notice, and it is load-bearing for the 'skill transfers to today' argument. The OpenHydroNet Colab's 'fine-tune only static_embedding_fc' trick is plausible and the notebook exists, but I did not execute it and could not confirm it from the repo tree. Skariah & Suriyakala (2022) is confirmed by Crossref as 'Forecasting reservoir inflow combining Exponential smoothing, ARIMA, and LSTM models', Arabian Journal of Geosciences 15(14), July 2022, with OpenAlex reporting is_oa false and 11 citations (the sweep said 8, from Semantic Scholar - source-dependent and already drifting), so dead_end 14's refusal to quote its MAPE is correct and should be kept.

PRACTICAL NOTE FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THE INGESTERS. Three of the rejections above are silent-corruption risks rather than citation hygiene, and all three sit in step one of the recommended workflow: the GEFS APCP 6-hourly reset (double counting precipitation), the GRRR lead_time=0 identity (foresight leak), and the Open-Meteo ERA5 timezone/model defaults (up to 40% day-level differences in the bias-correction target). Each would produce a plausible-looking number that is wrong in the direction that flatters the project. Fix all three before any benefit-retention figure is computed.

SCORE. All 16 sources are live and materially support their core claim, so none is rejected outright - but 16 claim-level defects are, of which five are substantive: the Sudheer 9965/8800 modelled-versus-observed inversion, the inverted west-coast skill headline, the Nitha lead-time and season overreach, the GRRR lead-0 foresight leak, and the wrongly-closed IMD gridded-rainfall route. The rest are counts, date ranges, response shapes and irreproducible recipes. The sweep's core thesis - that NOAA GEFS on AWS plus the Kerala SLDC scrape makes an honest forecast-driven October 2021 replay possible, with GRRR as an independent discharge-side second arm - is verified and stands.
